commentary: No open positions right now, so today's call is simple: does anything on my own watchlist actually clear the bar it set for itself? Three of my four price alerts (ANET, GE, CRWD) are close to their levels but haven't actually confirmed - I'm not chasing proximity. The fourth, Datadog, did confirm: it reclaimed and held above $250 today on a real, dated analyst upgrade (JMP raising its target to $311), backed by strong fundamentals and genuine institutional buying, not just a bounce. I'm buying a modest position sized around the pre-earnings risk, and I've deliberately set the timeline to close out before Datadog's August 6th earnings report rather than gamble on that print. CrowdStrike has a genuinely interesting story brewing - AI systems attacking other AI systems is pushing analysts to name it a top beneficiary - but the stock hasn't actually confirmed a new entry point yet, so I'm watching, not buying. Same with Arista and GE: both are hovering right at levels I'd want to see confirmed with real volume before committing capital. The market itself looks fine - stocks are above their long-term trend lines and credit markets are calm - but the strongest momentum names are cooling off a bit as a group, so I'm favoring one clear, catalyst-backed idea over chasing several marginal ones.

  for disciplined sizing, not for skipping the trade outright (no accompanying deterioration in
  fundamentals or price structure).
- Next earnings 2026-08-06 sits inside a normal swing window. Options market is pricing real
  event risk: ATM IV 73.5% (elevated), expected move ±9.7% into 7/31 expiry, put skew 6.2pp
  over calls (`skew_read: puts_bid_over_calls`), and the book's own `swing_playbook` explicitly
  says to prefer trading AFTER the print when the thesis isn't the binary itself. My thesis
  here is the ongoing infra-software re-rate (JMP catalyst), NOT an earnings bet — so per
  CLAUDE.md's "around vs through" default, I am sizing this as an AROUND-the-print trade: a
  14-day horizon that closes out before 8/6, not a hold-through-earnings position.
- Stock is only 8.6% below its 52-week high — limited technical room before this becomes
  a fresh-high breakout rather than a basing reclaim; if $250 fails again on volume this idea
  is wrong fast.
- Live price could not be pulled from blocked local feeds; I cross-verified the reclaim via two
  independent web sources rather than trading on the stale $254.79/$248.46 bundle bars, per the
  "verify before chasing a trigger" freshness rule. I am using a conservative entry ceiling
  below the higher of the two verified prints to avoid chasing.

**Earnings path:** AROUND the 8/6 print — 14-day horizon, explicit time-boxed invalidator to
force a decision before the print rather than holding through the binary.

**Variant perception:** Consensus is already `strong_buy` with 46 analysts and a stale mean
target only ~6.6% above the pre-catalyst price — the Street likes the business but had not
repriced the acceleration. My view: JMP's fresh +38% target hike (to $311, specifically citing
infra-software outperforming apps-software) is a leading data point, not the consensus. The
mechanism: sell-side models anchored on last quarter's 45.9% yoy growth understate how much of
that growth is AI-workload observability attach rather than legacy infra monitoring — if the
8/6 print shows accelerating net-new ARR / RPO from AI-native customers, the rest of the Street
re-rates toward JMP's number the way it has not yet. Resolution: the 8/6/2026 Q2 print (product
revenue growth, net new ARR, RPO) and whether other sell-side targets follow JMP's move in the
following weeks.

See JSON block. One BUY (DDOG), sized conservatively (~70% of the full risk-based budget,

fallback (even just a single quote endpoint) baked into the gather step when yfinance fails
would remove that manual step and reduce the risk of an out-of-date entry price on exactly the
runs where freshness matters most.

The result is that the entire macro narrative of the session was dropped: not one headline about the US–Iran strikes that have crude up 6.55% in five sessions, and consequently `market_events.flags.counts.geopolitical` scored **0** on a night with a ten-day ceasefire proposal live. A required regime input returned a confident false negative, and I only caught it because I ran outside web research. Two cheap fixes: (1) **stratify the headline cap** — reserve half the slots for market-wide/macro stories and half for single-name, instead of sorting purely by recency; (2) **collapse templated Benzinga movers lists** ("N [Sector] Stocks Moving In...") into one row before the cap, since they are structurally guaranteed to be the newest items every evening and currently crowd out everything that matters. ** the watchlist trigger checker is **direction-blind**, and that is what produced this run's false positive. My published PANW condition was a *reclaim* of ~$345 that *holds*; the alert fired because price came within 2% of $345 **from below** (live $340.12, -2.45% on the day) — the opposite of the stated condition. This is the same class of defect as LP-4566902391 (the AMD alert firing 3.9% off the level). Fix: parse a relation token out of `would_buy_at` — "reclaim / above / breaks out / closes above" requires price **at or above** the level, "pullback to / near / dip to / below" requires price **at or below** — and only fire when the relation is satisfied, defaulting to proximity-only with an explicit `relation: unknown` tag when no token parses. Secondary, same block: the alert quoted PANW's stale 7/20 close ($348.66) while `live_prices.json`, written four minutes earlier, carried $340.12 — the alert rows should quote the same live mark the `trigger_run_note` claims to have confirmed on, or the two blocks will keep contradicting each other on exactly the days a trigger matters.

** Two concrete data defects cost me real research time and nearly cost me a bad trade.

`gap_analysis` reports a gap's size, direction, and whether it later filled, but not how the session actually closed relative to its open — so UNH shows an unfilled +7.4% gap while `pct_change_1d` is only +1.16%, meaning most of the pop was sold intraday, and I had to infer that from two fields that don't reconcile on their face. A `close_vs_open_pct` (or an `intraday_fade` flag) on the gap object would let an evening review distinguish a *held* gap from a *faded* one, which is the entire difference between a real drift setup and a failed print — precisely the call I had to hedge on UNH tonight. Secondary: `momentum_health` was absent from this bundle entirely (not even `unknown`), and `position_histories` was `skipped`, so two documented inputs to the regime read were silently missing rather than explicitly null.
